citations.text: The study was approved by an independent ethics committee at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital in Gothenburg, Sweden (8883-12, 20121212) and registered at the Swedish National Database of Research and Development (identifier 113021; November 4, 2012; http://www.researchweb.org/is/vgr/project/113021).

Between March 2013 and July 2015, the ambulance or primary care teams identified 822 eligible patients.
Primary outcome was decline in functional activity ADLs assessed by the ADL Staircase 3 months after discharge from hospital.
The primary outcome was decline in functional activity, assessed by the ADL Staircase, from the index hospitalization until 3 months after discharge.
A one-step decline on the ADL Staircase – that is, loss of independence in one or more ADLs – was considered clinically relevant.

Associations of the intervention with the primary and secondary outcomes were assessed by either Cox regression or a multiple logistic regression model adjusted for relevant prognostic variables (sex, age, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index score).
Age, sex, and Charlson Comorbidity Index score were potential confounders and used as covariates.
Patients were excluded from the analysis if information of ADL score was missing at index and/or follow-up.

other_measurements.label: ADL Staircase before discharge
named: ADL independence/dependence was assessed by using the ADL Staircase before discharge.31

other_measurements.label: ADL classified into independence, IADL-dependence, and PADL-dependence
named: In a complementary analysis, the functional abilities of patients were classified into independence, IADL-dependence, and PADL-dependence.
result: When ADLs were classified in three strata (independence, IADL-dependence, and PADL-dependence), changes to a more dependence-associated stratum were less prevalent in the intervention group [11 (6.3%); n=176] than in the control group [33 (20.2%); n=163; P=0.0001].

other_measurements.label: ADL by Katz Index after 3 months (sample size basis)
named: The sample size calculation was based on change in functional capacity measured as the loss of basal ADL according to the Katz Index after 3 months (significance level 0.05, power 80%).
second_look: At the 3-month follow-up, decline in ADLs according to the ADL Staircase was less prevalent in the intervention group [24 (14.1%); n=170] than in the control group 98 (63.6%); n=154; P<0.0001, [Table 2].

planned: Associations of the intervention with the primary and secondary outcomes were assessed by either Cox regression or a multiple logistic regression model adjusted for relevant prognostic variables (sex, age, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index score).
The analysis used the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle – that is, the included patients remained in the study group to which they were allocated.
reported: In multiple logistic regression analyses, treatment in a CGA unit was independently associated with lower risk of a decline in ADLs (odds ratio [OR] 0.093; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.052–0.16; Table 3).
